1.description: Par 4, 342/323/307 yd. Men's 9-hole handicap 8 (18-hole HCP 16 on the North/South card). The only hole-specific note is from a Greenskeeper.org reviewer (roarksown1, 02/22/21) who played 'a twilight nine at the Mountaingate North course'. While complaining that the greens were quick and hard to hold, they wrote 'Some are also very small, like the first hole.' So the source supports only one thing: the green is very small. No source describes the hole's shape, elevation or hazards. Caveat: the reviewer probably started on North 1, but the review does not say so.

2.elevation: Steep hillside behind the green, so a long miss leaves a downhill chip or putt running fast toward the front. The green tilts away from a player above and behind it, i.e. back-to-front toward the tee.
hazards: very deep front greenside bunker that the green horseshoes (wraps) around
steep bank or hill behind (long) the green
green very wide but shallow (not deep)
2.description: Par 3, 189/169/153 yd, men's 9-hole HCP 5. Golf Top 18's North/South review (last reviewed 2004) describes it as a par three with 'a very wide green that seems to horseshoe around a very deep and unforgiving bunker'. Any shot hit long ends up on a steep hill, pitching to a green that runs severely away from the player. A Greenskeeper.org North 9 tip (Daddy_IRS) agrees: the green is wide but not deep, so a high shot helps it stop; a deep bunker guards the front; from long, the chip or putt is downhill and fast; distance control is essential. WARNING: a search-engine summary wrongly tied a 'hidden lake to the right of the fairway about 80 yards from the green' to this hole. On the Golf Top 18 page that sentence belongs to SOUTH hole 2, not North 2.

3.description: Par 4, 346/323/298 yd, men's 9-hole HCP 3. Greenskeeper.org North 9 tip (Daddy_IRS): 'Tee shot don't go left stay middle-right.' Bunkers surround the green and the green is small, so check your distance and keep the approach below the hole. The source does not say what the trouble on the left is (it gives no type for the left-side hazard). 'Keep it below the hole' suggests a back-to-front sloping green, but that is an inference, not stated.

10.description: Card: Par 4, 417/391/366 yd, SI 15 (Golfify and golfingrecord cards, which match the 6,719-yd rating). I found no written description of this hole. A captioned SkyGolf blog photo (2013, 'South Course: #1 Hole 417 yds Par 4') looks from a raised tee down a tree-lined fairway that drops into a valley. The cart path is on the left and a bunkered green is in the distance. Not from a written source (OSM + project DEM): the hole line plays east and bends slightly right (+16 deg) about 260 yd out. It falls about 35 m tee to green on build/backdrop_dem.tif (2 m). OSM bunkers: fairway right about 175 yd, left about 235 yd, left near the green about 388 yd, and 1 greenside right. Houses sit north of the hole past the cart path, so OB is possible there but unverified.

11.description: Card: Par 4, 400/387/359 yd, SI 1 (hardest hole on the N/S card). GolfTop18 (last reviewed 2004) calls it the best hole on the course. It is a par 4 that winds left around a canyon from tee to green, and the player has to cut off some of the canyon to leave a reasonable approach. The green sits out on a peninsula with bunkers around it and canyon short, left and long. A hidden lake lies right of the fairway about 80 yd from the green, so even a layup has to avoid it. SkyGolf blog (2013) describes a 400-yd par 4: a severe, almost U-shaped dogleg with a ravine to carry on the second shot to a well-protected green. CONFLICT: SkyGolf calls it a dogleg RIGHT. The GolfTop18 text, the OSM hole line (-59 deg turn) and aerial imagery all show it turning LEFT: the tee is at the north, the fairway runs south beside a wooded canyon on the player's left (east), then turns left (east) to the green. Treat it as a dogleg left. SkyGolf photos: from the tee, a brushy ravine and trees are on the left and the fairway is on the right; the approach photo shows the green beyond a brush-filled ravine with three bunkers across its front. The 'hidden lake' matches a triangular pond that OSM does not map. It sits about 80 yd short of the green and about 45-65 yd right of the line, at roughly UTM11N 363397E 3774557N (lon -118.48095, lat 34.10291). A second pond, which OSM does map (way 950199971), lies about 100 yd right, further south. OSM bunkers: 3 greenside (1 left, 2 right) and 1 fairway bunker right about 243 yd.

12.description: Card: Par 3, 174/153/97 yd, SI 13. GolfTop18 (2004): a par 3 with a nerve-racking approach that puts a premium on accuracy. Canyon lies short, left and long. Right looks safe, but a ball that goes too far right runs down a hill into the hidden lake. The green is relatively flat. SkyGolf blog (2013) has photos taken from the 3rd tee that look down on the I-405 and out to Westwood and the Getty Center, so the tee sits high on the canyon rim. Its photos of the hole show the green across a brush-covered canyon, with bunkers on the front-left and a large tree behind. A GolfNow/GolfPass photo ('hole #3 at South Course') shows the green on a ridge with bunkers on both sides and a drop-off with city views beyond. OSM: the line plays straight SSW. There are 3 greenside bunkers (2 left, 1 right). The OSM-mapped pond (way 950199971) is about 39 yd right of the line near the green (about 163 yd from the tee) and downhill. DEM: tee about 356 m, green about 353 m, canyon floor about 340 m between them.

13.description: Card: Par 4, 365/356/224 yd, SI 9. The 224-yd forward tee suggests it sits past the pond and the corner. GolfTop18 (2004): a pretty tee shot where the player can cut off more of the corner to leave a shorter, better-angled approach to an elevated green. GolfTop18 does not say which way it bends; the OSM line bends LEFT about 28 deg about 180 yd out. SkyGolf photos (2013): the tee shot crosses native brush and a ravine to a fairway beyond. The green photo shows a large shaped front bunker, the cart path on the left and pampas grass on the right. OSM: the back-tee line crosses the mapped pond (way 950199971) about 39-56 yd from the tee, a short forced carry. Fairway bunkers frame the corner: left about 188 and 234 yd, right about 197 and 222 yd. There is 1 greenside bunker on the right. DEM: green about 3 m above the tee.

18.description: Card: Par 5, 562/540/481 yd, SI 3, the longest hole on N/S. Older GolfPass and OpenGolfAPI cards list a 412-yd par 4; the 2013 SkyGolf caption, the current card and OSM all say par 5. SkyGolf blog (2013): a 562-yd par 5 with a severe 90-degree dogleg. The side of the hill runs along one side of the fairway and the fairway slopes away on the other. CONFLICT: SkyGolf says dogleg RIGHT with the hill on the right. Its own tee photo shows the brushy hill (houses on top) on the LEFT. OSM (-40 deg on the line; the fairway bends harder) and imagery show the hole turning LEFT, with the hillside and houses on the left/SW. Treat it as a dogleg left. Greenskeeper reviewer roarksown1 (Aug 2016) played South first and then North. While criticising the South nine (sloping fairways, awkward tee angles, lost-ball areas), he complained about finishing a nine on a par 5 where a perfectly struck driver rolls down a hill. That almost certainly means this hole, but he does not number it. SkyGolf approach photo: green with bunkers left and right, buildings (clubhouse area) behind. The photo looking back from the green shows the fairway falling away, so the green sits well above the landing area. DEM: tee about 365 m, dips slightly about 140 yd out, then climbs to the green at about 388 m (+23 m). OSM maps only 2 greenside bunkers (left, right). Imagery shows about 3 fairway bunkers on the outside (right) of the corner and about 2 more on the right of the second leg, none of them in OSM.
